senses.en: someone opposed to violence as a means of settling disputes

examples.text: As a committed pacifist, she refused to join the army even when conscription was introduced.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 pacifiste에서 왔으며, pacific(평화로운)에 -ist가 붙었습니다.

senses.en: To mollify, placate or soothe (someone or something).

examples.text: The manager offered a full refund to pacify the furious customer.

senses.en: fight violence and try to establish peace in (a location)

examples.text: The U.N. troops are working to pacify Bosnia

origin.ko: 중세 프랑스어 pacifier에서 왔고, 라틴어로 '평화(pāx)를 만들다'입니다.

senses.en: An enthusiastic expression of praise.

examples.text: The review was a paean to the novelist's gift for capturing everyday life.

origin.ko: 그리스어 Paián은 의술의 신 아폴론에게 바치던 승전 찬가였습니다. 여기서 열렬한 찬사를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: characterized by extreme care and great effort

examples.text: The restorers did painstaking work to repair the fragile frescoes.

origin.ko: pains(수고)와 taking(들이다)을 합친 말로, 수고를 아끼지 않는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Tolerable, acceptable.

examples.text: The agreement was palatable to both of them.

senses.en: Pleasing to the taste, tasty.

examples.text: The hospital tried to make its meals more palatable for patients.

senses.en: suitable for or like a palace

examples.text: palatial furnishings

origin.ko: 라틴어 palātium '궁전'에서 왔고, 로마 팔라티누스 언덕에 황제의 궁전이 있었습니다.

senses.en: loud and confused and empty talk

examples.text: The senator's speech was mostly palaver, offering no concrete plan for reform.

senses.en: influence or urge by gentle urging, caressing, or flattering

examples.text: He palavered her into going along

senses.en: Mentally draining activity, either physical or fuss.

examples.text: What a palaver!

origin.ko: 포르투갈어 palavra '말'에서 왔고, 라틴어 parabola '비유'가 원형입니다. 선원 은어로 쓰이다가 쓸데없는 수다를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: a manuscript (usually written on papyrus or parchment) on which more than one text has been written with the earlier writing incompletely erased and still visible

examples.text: Scholars used ultraviolet light to read the original prayer book beneath the medieval palimpsest.

senses.en: Something bearing the traces of an earlier, erased form.

examples.text: The old city is a palimpsest, with Roman walls still visible beneath its medieval streets.

origin.ko: 그리스어 palímpsēstos '다시 긁어낸'에서 왔습니다. 쓴 글을 긁어내고 다시 쓴 양피지입니다.

senses.en: lose strength or effectiveness; become or appear boring, insipid, or tiresome (to)

examples.text: the course palled on her

senses.en: Something that covers or surrounds like a cloak; in particular, a cloud of dust, smoke, etc., or a feeling of fear, gloom, or suspicion.

examples.text: The early election results cast a pall over what was supposed to be a celebration.

origin.ko: appall(맥이 빠지게 하다)이 줄어든 말로 보입니다. 힘이 빠져 시들해지고 싫증난다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of

examples.text: The company tried to palliate its mistake with a hasty apology.

senses.en: provide physical relief, as from pain

examples.text: The drug does not cure the disease but can palliate its worst symptoms.

origin.ko: 라틴어 palliō '망토로 덮다'에서 왔고, pallium은 '망토'입니다. 문제를 망토로 덮어 가볍게 보이게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: abnormally deficient in color as suggesting physical or emotional distress

examples.text: the pallid face of the invalid

senses.en: lacking in vitality or interest or effectiveness

examples.text: The sequel was a pallid imitation of the original film.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pallidus '창백한'에서 왔으며 pale과 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment

examples.text: There was a palpable sense of relief in the room after the verdict.

senses.en: Capable of being touched, felt or handled; touchable, tangible.

examples.text: Osric: A hit, a very palpable hit.

origin.ko: 라틴어 palpābilis에서 왔고, palpō는 '부드럽게 만지다'입니다. 손으로 만질 수 있을 만큼 뚜렷하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: beat rapidly

examples.text: His heart palpitated

senses.en: shake with fast, tremulous movements

examples.text: His nostrils palpitated

origin.ko: 라틴어 palpitō '떨다, 두근거리다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A solution to all problems.

examples.text: A monorail will be a panacea for our traffic woes.

origin.ko: 그리스어 panákeia '모든 것을 고치는'에서 왔습니다. 모든 병과 문제를 해결하는 만병통치약입니다.

senses.en: distinctive and stylish elegance

examples.text: The pianist performed the difficult concerto with remarkable panache.

origin.ko: 프랑스어로 '투구에 꽂은 깃털 장식'이라는 뜻입니다. 깃털을 꽂은 듯 멋과 기세가 있는 모습이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A formal speech publicly praising someone or something.

examples.text: The biography reads less like history than a long panegyric to the founder.

senses.en: formally expressing praise

examples.text: The critic's panegyric tone left no room for any real criticism.

origin.ko: 그리스어 panēgyrikos '대중 집회의'에서 왔습니다. 모두가 모인 자리에서 하는 칭송 연설입니다.

senses.en: a complete and impressive array

examples.text: The festival offered a dazzling panoply of music, dance, and street food.

senses.en: Something that covers and protects.

examples.text: A panoply of legal safeguards protects whistleblowers from retaliation.

origin.ko: 그리스어 panoplía '갑옷 한 벌'에서 왔습니다. 완전히 갖춘 장비 일체라는 뜻이 화려한 총집합으로 이어졌습니다.

senses.en: A short narrative illustrating a lesson (usually religious/moral) by comparison or analogy.

examples.text: The teacher used a parable about a lost sheep to illustrate forgiveness.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parabolḗ '비교'에서 왔습니다. 두 가지를 나란히 놓고 견주어 교훈을 주는 이야기입니다.

senses.en: A pattern, a way of doing something; especially a pattern of thought, a system of beliefs, a conceptual framework.

examples.text: Darwin's theory overturned the dominant paradigm of fixed species.

senses.en: a standard or typical example

examples.text: The Roman Republic became a paradigm of balanced government for later political thinkers.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parádeigma '본보기'에서 왔습니다. 옆에 놓고 견주도록 보여 주는 모범 틀이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: of or relating to a typical example

examples.text: Her career is paradigmatic of the struggles facing first-generation immigrants.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 paradigmatique에서 왔고, 그리스어 '본보기'가 원형입니다.

senses.en: A counterintuitive conclusion or outcome.

examples.text: It is an interesting paradox that drinking a lot of water can often make you feel thirsty.

senses.en: A person or thing having contradictory properties.

examples.text: He is a paradox; you would not expect him in that political party.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parádoxos '예상 밖의'에서 왔습니다. 통념에서 벗어난 의견이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: seemingly contradictory but nonetheless possibly true

examples.text: it is paradoxical that standing is more tiring than walking

origin.ko: paradox(통념에서 벗어난 의견)에 -ical이 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: model of excellence or perfection of a kind; one having no equal

examples.text: In the novel, Constanza is a paragon of virtue who would never compromise her reputation.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 paragonare '시금석에 대어 시험하다'에서 왔습니다. 시금석에 대도 가장 뛰어난 본보기라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Miscellaneous items, especially the set of equipment required for a particular activity.

examples.text: He has an impressive collection of bicycling paraphernalia, but he doesn't ride very often anymore.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어로 아내가 지참금 외에 가져오는 개인 재산을 가리켰습니다. 여기서 이런저런 개인 용품 일체가 되었습니다.

senses.en: To reduce, diminish or trim gradually something as if by cutting off.

examples.text: Albert had to pare his options down by disregarding anything beyond his meager budget.

senses.en: remove the skin from

examples.text: Victor pared some apples in preparation to make a tart.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 parer '다듬다'에서 왔고, 라틴어 parō '준비하다'가 원형입니다. 겉을 깎아 다듬는 데서 점차 줄이다가 되었습니다.

senses.en: qualifying or explaining; placed or as if placed in parentheses

examples.text: The author's parenthetical remarks often contain the sharpest insights in the essay.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parénthetos '곁에 끼워 넣은'에서 왔습니다. 문장 안에 덧붙여 넣은 설명이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a person who is rejected (from society or home)

examples.text: After the scandal, the once-admired banker became a social pariah.

origin.ko: 타밀어 paṟaiyar에서 왔고, 원래 북(paṟai)을 치던 낮은 신분의 사람들을 가리켰습니다. 여기서 사회에서 배척당하는 사람이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Equality; comparability of strength or intensity.

examples.text: Women's groups are demanding pay parity with their male colleagues.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pār '같은, 동등한'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A conference, especially one between enemies.

examples.text: The two commanders met under a white flag for a brief parley.

senses.en: discuss, as between enemies

examples.text: The rebels agreed to parley with government envoys before the deadline.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 parler '말하다'에서 왔습니다. 적과 마주 앉아 말로 풀어 보는 회담입니다.

senses.en: narrowly restricted in outlook or scope

examples.text: little sympathy with parochial mentality

senses.en: relating to or supported by or located in a parish

examples.text: parochial schools

origin.ko: 그리스어 pároikos '이웃'에서 온 교구라는 말입니다. 한 교구의 좁은 범위에 갇혀 시야가 좁다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A work or performance that imitates another work or performance with ridicule or irony.

examples.text: The cabaret's parody of the president's speech had the audience roaring with laughter.

senses.en: To make a parody of something.

examples.text: The comedy movie parodied the entire Western genre.

origin.ko: 그리스어 parōidía '곁에서 부르는 노래'에서 왔습니다. 원작 옆에서 흉내 내어 부르며 풍자하는 작품입니다.

senses.en: avoid or try to avoid fulfilling, answering, or performing (duties, questions, or issues)

examples.text: The minister parried every question about the budget deficit.

senses.en: To avoid, deflect, or ward off (an attack, a blow, an argument, etc.).

examples.text: She parried the blow with her forearm and stepped back.

origin.ko: 라틴어 parāre '막다, 준비하다'에서 중세 라틴어와 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 공격을 막아 받아넘긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: excessively unwilling to spend

examples.text: The parsimonious heir counted every coin and refused to hire any household help.

senses.en: Using a minimal number of assumptions, steps, or conjectures.

examples.text: Scientists prefer the more parsimonious explanation when two theories fit the data equally well.

origin.ko: 라틴어 parsimonia '절약'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Biased in favor of a person, side, or point of view, especially when dealing with a competition or dispute.

examples.text: God is not partial; he does not play favorites.

senses.en: Existing as a part or portion; incomplete.

examples.text: So far, I have only pieced together a partial account of the incident.

senses.en: Having a predilection for something.

examples.text: not partial to an ostentatious display

origin.ko: 라틴어 pars '부분'에서 왔습니다. 전체가 아닌 한쪽 부분만 편드는 데서 '편파적인'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Preference, bias in favor of, tendency.

examples.text: The judge's partiality towards the defendant caused him to be replaced, with someone who was apparently more neutral.

senses.en: a predisposition to like something

examples.text: The old professor had a well-known partiality for strong black tea.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 partiālitās에서 왔으며, 부분(한쪽)만 편드는 성향을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: Devoted to or biased in support of a party, group, or cause.

examples.text: partisan politics

senses.en: a fervent and even militant proponent of something

examples.text: The senator remained a fierce partisan of tax reform throughout her career.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 partigiano '한 편의 옹호자'에서 왔고, parte는 '부분, 편'입니다.

senses.en: a person who has suddenly risen to a higher economic status but has not gained social acceptance of others in that class

examples.text: Old-money families looked down on the parvenu who had bought the estate.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 parvenir '도달하다'의 과거분사로, 라틴어 perveniō '이르다'가 원형입니다. 갑자기 높은 자리에 올라선 사람입니다.

senses.en: a section of text; particularly a section of medium length

examples.text: The test asks students to read a short passage and summarize its central argument.

senses.en: The advance of time.

examples.text: The passage of decades has not erased the value of parental monitoring.

senses.en: the passing of a law by a legislative body

examples.text: The company was one of the prime movers in lobbying for the passage of the act.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 passage에서 왔고, passer '지나가다'에서 나왔습니다. 글 속을 지나가는 한 구간이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: out of fashion

examples.text: Critics claimed that the grand narrative style had become passe by the 1980s.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 passé '지나간'에서 왔습니다. 시대가 지나간 한물간 것이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An incongruous mixture; a hodgepodge.

examples.text: The house failed to attract a buyer because the decor was a pastiche of Bohemian and Scandinavian styles.

senses.en: a work of art that imitates the style of some previous work

examples.text: The film is a loving pastiche of 1940s detective stories.

origin.ko: 이탈리아어 pasticcio '여러 재료를 섞은 파이'에서 왔습니다. 이것저것 섞은 짜깁기라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (used with regard to idealized country life) idyllically rustic

examples.text: The painter's pastoral landscapes show sheep grazing beside quiet streams.

senses.en: a literary work idealizing the rural life (especially the life of shepherds)

examples.text: Virgil's pastoral poems helped establish a lasting literary tradition.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pāstōrālis '목자의'에서 왔고, pāstor는 '양치기'입니다. 양치기가 있는 목가적 전원을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment

examples.text: It was patent to everyone in the room that the witness was lying.

senses.en: a document granting an inventor sole rights to an invention

examples.text: The firm filed a patent for its new battery design.

origin.ko: 라틴어 patēns '열린, 명백한'에서 왔고, pateō는 '열려 있다'입니다. 활짝 열려 누구 눈에나 분명하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: able to cause disease

examples.text: While the environment is teeming with bacteria and fungi, most are not pathogenic.

origin.ko: patho-(병)와 -genic(~을 낳는)을 합친 말로, 병을 일으킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: caused by or evidencing a mentally disturbed condition

examples.text: a pathological liar

senses.en: caused by or altered by or manifesting disease or pathology

examples.text: The biopsy revealed pathological changes in the liver tissue.

origin.ko: 그리스어 páskhō '겪다'와 -logía '학문'에서 나온 말로, 병을 다루는 학문에서 병적인 상태를 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: the male head of family or tribe

examples.text: The family patriarch, aged ninety, still presided over every holiday dinner.

senses.en: A founder of a political or religious movement, an organization or an enterprise.

examples.text: He is regarded as the patriarch of modern environmental policy.

origin.ko: 그리스어 patriárkhēs '씨족의 창시자'에서 왔습니다. 아버지 같은 가문의 우두머리라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: belonging to or characteristic of the nobility or aristocracy

examples.text: Her patrician bearing and clipped accent marked her as old money.

senses.en: a member of the aristocracy

examples.text: The emperor elevated several loyal families to the status of patricians.

origin.ko: 라틴어 patricius에서 왔고, 로마 원로원 의원 '아버지들(patrēs)'에서 나온 말입니다. 로마 귀족 계층을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: To treat condescendingly; to talk down to.

examples.text: Please don't patronize me; I understand the contract perfectly well.

senses.en: To act as a patron of; to defend, protect, or support.

examples.text: Wealthy merchants patronized the young painter and funded his studies in Rome.

senses.en: To be a customer of (an establishment), especially a regular customer.

examples.text: Locals still patronize the old bakery on the corner every morning.

origin.ko: patron(후원자)에 -ize가 붙은 말입니다. 후원자인 양 아랫사람 대하듯 한다는 데서 깔보는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: (used of behavior or attitude) characteristic of those who treat others with condescension

examples.text: Her patronizing tone made the junior engineers feel their ideas were worthless.

senses.en: an insufficient quantity or number

examples.text: The study was criticized for the paucity of data supporting its conclusions.

origin.ko: 라틴어 paucitās '소수, 부족'에서 왔고, paucus는 '적은'입니다.
